dossier.public_summary: A 3.5 Earth-size dip repeats every 0.56 days exactly at the star's 0.565-day starspot spin, with strong starspot modulation and a large phase curve near depth. The dip is much longer than expected for this small M dwarf, so stellar variability best explains it rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Ultra-short 0.565 d period exactly matches star's measured spot rotation; 2.6% dip is tiny compared to ~1-2% spot modulation, so dip can be spot-related harmonic alias rather than independent orbit.
Very large out-of-transit swing (74% of transit depth) at same period as rotation, not expected for 3.47 Rearth planet, positively indicates spots/close binary ellipsoidal variation.
Duration 1.478 h is 1.68x central transit for TIC R=0.443 Rsun (M dwarf) and density mismatch dominates fit, inconsistent with central planet transit; shape flat but long.
Dip is on target so not a neighbour blend, but flat-bottom V and low xgboost planet_rank 0.08 favour spotted/eclipsing binary on target over planet despite similar planet matches.
